author: Hernán Cortés; ed. Francisco Antonio Lorenzana
publisher: Imprenta del Superior Gobierno de Joseph Antonio de Hogal
volume_or_location: single folio volume; frontispiece position varies in surviving copies
notes: University of Granada identifies the calcographic frontispiece as Hernán Cortés kneeling and offering an orb symbolizing the conquered territory to Charles V, accompanied by Indigenous figures. Christie's records a copy in which the frontispiece was bound deep in the preliminary/text sequence rather than at the normal opening, making it a useful binding-state case.

author: Antonio de Solís y Ribadeneyra
work: Historia de la conquista de México
notes: Auction and catalogue descriptions explicitly identify the Cortés portrait as the frontispiece; a separate portrait of Antonio de Solís and numerous historical plates/maps follow. The edition therefore opens with the historical agent rather than the historian-author.

author: Francesco Saverio Clavigero; English translation
publisher: G. G. J. and J. Robinson
artist_or_engraver: cartographic engravers unresolved in current evidence
notes: Library of Congress states explicitly that the frontispiece in each volume is a map: vol. I Anahuac/Mexico and neighboring kingdoms as in 1521; vol. II the Lakes of Mexico. The 1780-81 Italian original is catalogued with plates/maps/title vignette but no currently confirmed formal frontispiece, so translation-state comparison is high priority.

author: Voltaire; English translation
work: The History of Charles XII, King of Sweden
notes: Sir John Soane's Museum catalogue gives an engraved frontispiece portrait of Charles XII plus a folding map; this is a reissue of the second English edition with reset title page.

author: Voltaire
work: Histoire de Charles XII, Roi de Suède
notes: Bibliographical/auction evidence records an unsigned engraved portrait of Charles XII as frontispiece and a separate engraved title vignette, a clean example of the distinction between the two functions.
